text.p: Italy's debt market ended firmer, rising in the wake of firmer T-Bonds which boosted all other European markets.

"The Bund was very strong today and touched new highs but the Btp future seemed to be having a bit more difficulty in rising. At these levels operators are wary about buying," one trader said. "Some are taking profits before going on summer holiday," he added.
The 10-year Btp/Bund spread remained over 90 basis points.

Traders said the direction of the Italian market will be given by foreign markets with no domestic factors to give impetus now that talks on streamlining the country's welfare state system have been put off to September.
"Thursday sees U.S. second quarter GDP data and this could be an occasion to move a fairly static market," one broker said, noting however that the Italian market tone was positive.
In cash bonds, the February 2007 Btp gained 48 basis points to 102.96, yielding 6.42 percent. The Btp/Bund spread was at 94 bps against 97 bps at the previous close.
On Thursday the Italian Treasury auctions three and five-year Btps.
